title: Maximum Distance Between a Pair of Values
summary: Given two non-increasing integer arrays nums1 and nums2, find the maximum distance of a valid pair (i, j) where i <= j and nums1[i] <= nums2[j].
statement: Given two non-increasing integer arrays nums1 and nums2, find the maximum distance of a valid pair (i, j) where i <= j and nums1[i] <= nums2[j]. If no valid pairs exist, return 0.
constraints: A valid pair has i<=j and nums1[i]<=nums2[j]; maximize j-i, returning zero if no positive distance exists.
hints: Monotonic order makes the smallest viable nums1 index move only forward.
Sweep nums2 by j while advancing i until nums1[i]<=nums2[j].
When i<=j, update the answer with j-i.
Once nums1[i] is too large for a decreasing nums2 value it remains unusable later; the earliest viable i gives the largest distance for each j.
editorial: Once nums1[i] is too large for a decreasing nums2 value it remains unusable later; the earliest viable i gives the largest distance for each j.

tests.explanation: Pair i=2,j=4 has distance two, which is maximum.
The farthest valid pair uses i=0,j=1 for distance one.
